claims.statement: A scheduled job runs on a separate job-id-derived cron thread under its own conversation lock; the host bounds it to 30 minutes and, after timeout, attempts interrupted-checkpoint recovery before propagating the failure to the scheduler.

For a cron-triggered invocation, BackgroundSubagents runs both local task delegation and remote start_async_task delegation inline in the scheduled graph turn, forbids nested delegation, and leaves no pending background job or later delivery route.

Inline cron delegation has a separate shared four-slot semaphore and 10-minute per-call deadline: excess fan-out queues, results are capped at 64,000 characters, and timeout or failure is returned as a bounded error ToolMessage so it cannot cause graph retries to replay sibling delegation.

Scheduled runs are unattended: the host invokes them without interactive approval or authorization handlers and prevents operator authority, while the runtime marks cron context and the middleware hides detached-worker management tools.

Talon is an experimental, alpha-status local runtime host for long-running Deep Agents; it is not intended for production or enterprise use and does not implement production-grade HITL policy, channel administrator controls, sandbox-backed isolation, or multi-tenant boundaries.

TalonHost owns one event loop's agent runtime, channel adapters, and optional scheduler; startup initializes the runtime, binds and starts channels, then starts the scheduler, while partial-start failure unwinds started components and shutdown cancels work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime.

The host keys a conversation by provider plus channel conversation ID, uses that root as the serialized graph-thread/reset key, and persists `/new` reset counters so the active thread receives a `:talon-reset:<n>` suffix.

A replacement channel message cancels the active turn and attempts interrupted-checkpoint recovery; it suppresses stale output through a generation check, propagates recovery failure as metadata, and blocks that conversation until restart if cancellation/recovery exceeds 30 seconds.

`ToolApprovalRequest` carries a conversation ID, the first interrupt ID, and all action requests awaiting a single approve/reject decision; it is supplied through the optional approval handler on `AgentRequest`.

The runtime validates unique nonempty interrupt IDs and nonempty mapping action requests before prompting, batches simultaneous protected actions into one decision, resumes each interrupt with a correctly sized decision list, and cancels MCP elicitation interrupts in the same resume command.
Cron, background-delivery, and handler-less requests auto-deny protected tool-approval batches rather than prompting; attended requests pass the complete batch to their handler.

The host records a pending approval per conversation and accepts text or reaction decisions only when they match the originating identity; reaction matching additionally checks the provider, conversation, prompt message, sender, and recognized emoji.

DeepAgentRuntime snapshots and captures its approval policy and graph per invocation; a changed policy rebuilds the graph for a later invocation, while invalid policy or graph construction failure leaves the previous graph/snapshot intact and blocks the attempted invocation.

Conversation archive tools receive their channel/chat scope from trusted invocation context, expose list/search/read operations, and search pages report semantic status, indexing status/pending state, opaque pagination, and expired cursors so incomplete retrieval is distinguishable from absent history.

The packaged default agent guidance treats retrieved content as evidence rather than instructions, asks the agent to group independent tool calls so approval applies to the entire batch, minimizes task capabilities/context, and explicitly states that defensive prompts are not a sandbox.

The CLI uses EchoAgentRuntime when no model is configured; otherwise it opens SQLite checkpoints and the configured archive, wraps them in ConversationSaver, loads MCP tools, constructs DeepAgentRuntime, and attaches PersistentCronScheduler when channels are present.

TalonConfig namespaces assistant state by a validated assistant ID, creates the home and state directories with mode 0700, initializes the tool-approval store, and keeps the checkpoint database and conversation-reset state inside that home.
Talon ships WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord channel adapters; their shared exposure policy supports self, allowlist, and open modes, and open mode requires an explicit risk acknowledgement.

MCPToolProvider loads configured MCP tools together with status, authorization, reload, and configuration-management tools, rejects management-name collisions, and serializes reloads; runtime MCP replacement builds a new graph before assigning new tools so a failed replacement retains the prior graph and tool set.

An interactive MCP authorization flow is bound to the initiating provider, channel conversation, and sender; it rejects expired or concurrent flows and accepts a callback URL only from that same identity.

PersistentCronScheduler claims a due job by advancing its next run before invocation, marks successful or failed runs, suppresses delivery for the silent sentinel, and logs then retries a failed scan on the normal tick interval.
Cron management tools are scoped to the current invocation's trusted origin and support relative one-shot or recurring schedules plus IANA-timezone wall-clock one-shot and daily schedules.

Ordinary chat delegation stores workers and pending results only in memory; the host dispatches completed results only when the owner conversation is idle and starts an unattended background-delivery turn, while shutdown and conversation cancellation cancel workers.
